acceptanceCriteria: TestAggregateCaptureSignalHelper exits within a bounded time after its parent test process dies (shown by a test or scripted check that kills the parent with SIGKILL), without weakening the signal-capture assertions.
A note records whether other self-exec helpers in the repo share the unbounded-wait pattern; any found are filed or fixed together.
body: Observed 2026-10-16 09:51 CDT on Darwin arm64, Go 1.27.1, load average ~124: pid 94765 `localcompletion.test -test.run=^TestAggregateCaptureSignalHelper$ -test.v` (go-build3457301770) had elapsed 01-09:55, PPID 1 (reparented to launchd), state S, 0% CPU. The parent test (internal/localcompletion/storage_test.go ~102) starts it via groupreap.Start and stops it only in a deferred cleanup, so when the parent binary dies without running defers (timeout panic, SIGKILL, lane interruption), the helper blocks in signal.NotifyContext forever. Expected: the helper bounds its own lifetime (deadline env, parent-death detection such as a stdin pipe EOF or PPID check) so it exits once its parent is gone. Actual: indefinite orphan holding the fixture repo. The orphan was left in place, unkilled, as evidence.
title: localcompletion signal-capture test helper outlives its parent test binary (orphaned 33 h)
